t: You're on Euston Road, a busy thoroughfare in central London running from Marylebone Road across to King's Cross. It's part of the London Inner Ring Road, and it marks the edge of the congestion charge zone. The name comes from Euston Hall, the family seat of the Dukes of Grafton, who became major property owners in this area during the mid-nineteenth century. The cricketer William Edwards died here in 1947. He played two first-class matches for Kent in 1884.
